name: Read contacts
plain: Lets the app read the whole address book.
meaning: Exposes names, numbers, emails, and who a person knows. Apps use it to match friends, which also lets them upload the entire social graph of the person's family and colleagues.

android.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't allow (Allow only while using app is not offered for contacts group)
android.store_policy: Play: data-safety disclosure; uploading contacts needs prominent disclosure
android.note: Android 17 (API 37): Contacts Provider 2 removes account columns from the Data view and applies strict SQL when READ_CONTACTS is not held (apps targeting 37).

ios.prompt_ui: Allow Full Access, Limited Access (iOS 18), Don't Allow
ios.persistence: Until revoked; limited selection is per app
ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.1(iv) and 5.1.2: do not upload contacts without consent
ios.note: Notes field needs the com.apple.developer.contacts.notes entitlement (iOS 13).

limits.headline: Can see your whole address book once you tap Allow, or only some on iPhone
limits.user_action: You tap Find friends or Match my contacts
can: Upload the full list to match friends
Take a contact through the picker with no permission
cannot: See contacts before you tap Allow
Offer an Allow only while using choice for contacts on Android
See the Notes field on iPhone without Apple's entitlement
See account details on Android 17 apps that target the new version
limits.differs: iPhone with iOS 18 and later adds Limit Access; Android gives all or nothing for the contacts group.

story.what_it_is: Lets the app read your whole address book.
story.for_you: A prompt asks to access your contacts. If you allow it, the app can see the names, numbers and emails of everyone you know. They have not agreed to this.
story.for_makers: Contacts let apps grow fast by finding friends. They also feed caller ID, spam block and ad matching. That social map is powerful, so platforms limit it and review apps that ask.

use_cases.example: A chat app shows which of your friends already use it.
A photo app suggests people to follow.
A caller ID app names callers by matching against its database.
An ad network matches hashed phone numbers to build a profile.
A game links friends for leaderboards and team play.
A payment app lets you pay people without typing a number.
A dating app hides people you already know.

risks: Hashed numbers used for ad matching
story.android_note: Android 17 removes account columns from the contacts data view and tightens queries when the permission is missing.
story.ios_note: The Notes field needs an Apple entitlement. The rest of the address book comes with the permission.

technical_bounds: Contact picker avoids the permission on both platforms
iOS 18 lets people share a subset

abuse: Uploading entire address books for shadow profiles

linkedin.how: Address book upload fed People You May Know (policy 2.1). Contacts sync is now removed: LinkedIn help says it no longer supports syncing contacts and has started removing the feature (date not stated, pages updated about a year before Nov 2026). Members can still delete previously imported contacts. Play and Apple labels still list Contacts.

history.change: Limited contacts access and ContactAccessButton added
Contacts Provider 2 drops account columns from the Data view for apps targeting 37

refs.label: LinkedIn Help: Sync contacts from other address books no longer available
